candidate_relations.reason: Birth weight 2152 g at 35+4 weeks indicates growth restriction as an associated perinatal finding, not hydranencephaly.
Leigh syndrome is a metabolic basal-ganglia disease, not replacement of hemispheres by fluid after co-twin death.
Poor pupillary responses and optic pallor are ocular consequences of severe hemispheric loss, not Leber congenital amaurosis.

case_quality_flags: MRI shows hydranencephaly after co-twin demise; none of the three candidates names it.
